newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargoes quiet.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargoes quiet.

text.p: European high sulphur barges were largely steady on Wednesday in a quiet early market with thinner demand but supplies were also said to a be tighter with the absence of Russian material.

High sulphur fuel oil barges traded twice at $86 and once at $86.50 fob Rotterdam in the morning and mid-day talk was in the $86/$86.50, only 50 cents a tonne softer on the selling side. One trader said some independents were asking $87 per tonne.
Several traders said bunker demand was thinner than Tuesday, in the 6,000-9,000 tonne region and was not expected to grow considerably as the day progressed.
The supply picture was mixed with some saying there was no shortage of avails but others saying that the absence of Russian material meant supplies were a thinner.

"There's a little bit of a shortage as no Russian material is being shown...The Russians are asking too much for their stuff and Rotterdam is the cheapest area, I'm sure they want to sell somewhere else," one trader said.
The high sulphur fuel oil cargo market was reportedly quiet with traders saying that availability was there but Monday's deal at $81.75 fob was still keeping buyers at bit cautious.
The trade has prompted sellers to raise their asking price a few dollars to $84/$85 cif a tonne.
One trader, who said that the deal has shocked everyone in the market, added that he received offers early on Wednesday but "we did not go as far as discussing prices".
"I did not see weakness in the market but I also did not see any such strength," the trader said, commenting on Monday's deal.
